subject: Reasoning
q: Two clocks are set right at noon. One gains 2 minutes per hour and the other loses 1 minute per hour. How far apart will they be at 8 pm?
explanation: They drift apart by 2 + 1 = 3 minutes each hour; in 8 hours that is 24 minutes.

subject: Reasoning
q: A clock gains 3 minutes every hour. It was set right at 7:00 am. What is the correct time when it shows 1:18 pm?
explanation: The clock runs 63 minutes for every real hour. It shows 6 h 18 min = 378 minutes after 7:00, and 378 ÷ 63 = 6 real hours, so the correct time is 1:00 pm.

subject: Reasoning
q: If today is Tuesday, what day of the week will it be 45 days from today?
explanation: 45 = 6 weeks + 3 days, so count 3 days on from Tuesday. The answer is Friday.

subject: Reasoning
q: If today is Sunday, what day of the week was it 100 days ago?
explanation: 100 = 14 weeks + 2 days, so go back 2 days from Sunday. The answer is Friday.

subject: Reasoning
q: If the day after tomorrow is a Sunday, what was the day before yesterday?
explanation: Today is Friday (two days before Sunday), and two days before Friday is Wednesday. The answer is Wednesday.

subject: Reasoning
q: If three days ago it was Saturday, what day will it be four days after tomorrow?
explanation: Today is Tuesday; tomorrow is Wednesday, and four days after Wednesday is Sunday. The answer is Sunday.

subject: Reasoning
q: If the 5th of a month is a Monday, what day of the week is the 28th of that month?
explanation: The 28th is 23 days later: 3 weeks and 2 days after Monday. The answer is Wednesday.

subject: Reasoning
q: An examination is to be held 62 days after a Thursday. On which day of the week will it fall?
explanation: 62 = 8 weeks + 6 days; six days after Thursday is Wednesday. The answer is Wednesday.

subject: Reasoning
q: Today is Friday. What day of the week will it be 1000 days from today?
explanation: 1000 = 142 weeks + 6 days; six days after Friday is Thursday. The answer is Thursday.

subject: Reasoning
q: If yesterday was Wednesday, what day will it be 30 days after tomorrow?
explanation: Today is Thursday and tomorrow Friday; 30 days = 4 weeks + 2 days, and two days after Friday is Sunday. The answer is Sunday.

subject: Reasoning
q: The first day of a 31-day month is a Wednesday. On which day does the month end?
explanation: The 31st is 30 days after the 1st: 4 weeks and 2 days after Wednesday. The answer is Friday.

subject: Reasoning
q: If the 18th of a month falls on a Saturday, what day was the 1st of that month?
explanation: The 1st is 17 days earlier: 2 weeks and 3 days before Saturday. The answer is Wednesday.

subject: Reasoning
q: A meeting is held every 9 days. If one is held on a Monday, on what day will the fifth meeting after it fall?
explanation: The fifth meeting after it is 5 × 9 = 45 days later: 6 weeks and 3 days after Monday. The answer is Thursday.

subject: Reasoning
q: A patient takes a tablet every 36 hours, the first at 8 am on Monday. On which day is the fourth tablet taken?
explanation: The fourth tablet comes 3 × 36 = 108 hours = 4 days 12 hours after 8 am Monday, i.e. at 8 pm on Friday. The answer is Friday.

subject: Reasoning
q: Counting today as the first day, the 20th day will be a Saturday. What day is today?
explanation: The 20th day is 19 days after today; 19 = 2 weeks + 5 days, and five days before Saturday is Monday. The answer is Monday.

subject: Reasoning
q: If the 3rd of a month is a Friday, on what date does the third Monday of that month fall?
explanation: The first Monday is the 6th, so the third Monday is 6 + 14 = the 20th.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which of the following years was or will be a leap year?
explanation: A century year is a leap year only if it is divisible by 400; 2000 is, but 1800, 1900 and 2100 are not.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which one of these years was NOT a leap year?
explanation: 1900 is divisible by 100 but not by 400, so it was an ordinary year; the others are divisible by 4 and are not century years.

subject: Reasoning
q: How many leap years are there from 2001 to 2100, both years included?
explanation: The multiples of 4 from 2004 to 2100 number 25, but 2100 is not a leap year (not divisible by 400), leaving 24.

subject: Reasoning
q: How many days are there in the years 2023 and 2024 taken together?
explanation: 2023 has 365 days and 2024, a leap year, has 366: 731 in all.

subject: Reasoning
q: A child was born on 29 February 2008. In how many of the years from 2009 to 2020 did the date 29 February occur?
explanation: 29 February occurs only in leap years; between 2009 and 2020 these are 2012, 2016 and 2020, so 3.

subject: Reasoning
q: An ordinary (non-leap) year consists of 52 weeks and how many extra days?
explanation: 52 weeks make 364 days, and an ordinary year has 365 days, so there is 1 extra day.

subject: Reasoning
q: A leap year begins on a Thursday. Which days of the week occur 53 times in that year?
explanation: A leap year has 52 weeks and 2 days; the two extra days are the first two days of the year, Thursday and Friday.

subject: Reasoning
q: The last day of a century (such as 31 December 2000) can never fall on which of these days?
explanation: Over the 400-year Gregorian cycle, 31 December of a century year falls only on Sunday, Friday, Wednesday, Monday; it is never a Tuesday, Thursday or Saturday.

subject: Reasoning
q: In a leap year, which of these months always begins on the same day of the week as January?
explanation: From 1 January to 1 July in a leap year there are 31+29+31+30+31+30 = 182 days = exactly 26 weeks, so both months start on the same day.

subject: Reasoning
q: The calendar of 2021 can be used again, without change, in which year?
explanation: A calendar repeats when a year starts on the same weekday and has the same length; 2021 began on a Friday and so does 2027, both ordinary years.

subject: Reasoning
q: 14 August 1947 was a Thursday. What day of the week was 14 August 1948?
explanation: The year between includes 29 February 1948, so it has 366 days = 52 weeks + 2 days; so the day is Saturday.

subject: Reasoning
q: 1 January 2025 was a Wednesday. On what day did 1 January 2026 fall?
explanation: 2025 is an ordinary year of 365 days = 52 weeks + 1 day; so the day is Thursday.

subject: Reasoning
q: If 1 March of a year is a Monday, what day is 1 April of the same year?
explanation: March has 31 days = 4 weeks + 3 days; so the day is Thursday.

subject: Reasoning
q: 23 March 2024 was a Saturday. What day of the week was 23 March 2025?
explanation: No 29 February lies between these dates, so 365 days = 52 weeks + 1 day pass; so the day is Sunday.

subject: Reasoning
q: In an ordinary (non-leap) year, 1 January is a Monday. What day is 1 March?
explanation: January and February together have 31 + 28 = 59 days = 8 weeks + 3 days; so the day is Thursday.

subject: Reasoning
q: In a leap year whose 1 January is a Saturday, what day is 1 March?
explanation: January and February have 31 + 29 = 60 days = 8 weeks + 4 days; so the day is Wednesday.

subject: Reasoning
q: If 1 January 2000 was a Saturday, what day was 1 January 2001?
explanation: 2000 was a leap year (divisible by 400) of 366 days = 52 weeks + 2 days; so the day is Monday.

subject: Reasoning
q: In a certain year 14 August falls on a Sunday. On what day does 25 December fall in the same year?
explanation: From 14 August to 25 December is 17 + 30 + 31 + 30 + 25 = 133 days = exactly 19 weeks; so the day is Sunday.

subject: Reasoning
q: If 23 March falls on a Tuesday in some year, what day of the week is 14 August in that year?
explanation: From 23 March to 14 August is 8 + 30 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 14 = 144 days = 20 weeks + 4 days; so the day is Saturday.

subject: Reasoning
q: 5 June 2024 was a Wednesday. What day of the week was 5 June 2023?
explanation: Going back a year crosses 29 February 2024, i.e. 366 days = 52 weeks + 2 days back; so the day is Monday.

subject: Reasoning
q: If 15 January is a Tuesday, what day of the week is 15 February of that year?
explanation: January has 31 days = 4 weeks + 3 days; so the day is Friday.

subject: Reasoning
q: The first Monday of a month falls on the 3rd. On what date is the fourth Friday of that month?
explanation: If the 3rd is a Monday, the Fridays are the 7th, 14th, 21st, 28th; the fourth is the 28th.

subject: Reasoning
q: The 10th of a 30-day month is a Wednesday. How many Sundays does the month have?
explanation: If the 10th is a Wednesday, the Sundays are the 7th, 14th, 21st, 28th, so there are 4.

subject: Reasoning
q: A 31-day month begins on a Friday. Which days of the week occur five times in it?
explanation: 31 days = 4 weeks + 3 days, and the 3 extra days are the first three: Sunday, Friday and Saturday.

subject: Reasoning

explanation: In dictionary order the words run: Pleading, Pleasant, Pleasing, Pleasure.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which word comes third in dictionary order: Monarch, Monastery, Monetary, Monitor, Monolith?
explanation: In dictionary order the words run: Monarch, Monastery, Monetary, Monitor, Monolith.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which of these words would appear first in a dictionary: Candid, Candle, Candour, Candidate?
explanation: In dictionary order the words run: Candid, Candidate, Candle, Candour.

subject: Reasoning
q: Of Parliament, Parallel, Paramount, Parasite, which will come last in a dictionary?
explanation: In dictionary order the words run: Parallel, Paramount, Parasite, Parliament.

subject: Reasoning
q: If Estimate, Esteem, Establish, Estuary are arranged as in a dictionary, which one is in the second position?
explanation: In dictionary order the words run: Establish, Esteem, Estimate, Estuary.

subject: Reasoning
q: How many of the words Liberty, Library, Literacy, Lithium come before ‘Literal’ in a dictionary?
explanation: In dictionary order the words run: Liberty, Library, Literacy, Literal, Lithium.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which sequence puts these words in the order they appear in a dictionary? 1. Abstract  2. Absurd  3. Absorb  4. Absolute  5. Abstain
explanation: In dictionary order the words run: Absolute, Absorb, Abstain, Abstract, Absurd.

subject: Reasoning
q: When Tribunal, Tributary, Tribute, Tribulation are listed alphabetically, which word is second?
explanation: In dictionary order the words run: Tribulation, Tribunal, Tributary, Tribute.

subject: Reasoning
q: Pick the word that comes first alphabetically: Custom, Custody, Cushion, Cuisine.
explanation: In dictionary order the words run: Cuisine, Cushion, Custody, Custom.

subject: Reasoning
q: Put Refuse, Refute, Refund, Refuge in dictionary order. Which word is third?
explanation: In dictionary order the words run: Refuge, Refund, Refuse, Refute.

subject: Reasoning
q: When the words Dialogue, Diagram, Diameter, Dialect are arranged alphabetically, which two occupy the middle positions?
explanation: In dictionary order the words run: Diagram, Dialect, Dialogue, Diameter.

subject: Reasoning
q: In a dictionary, which of these comes immediately after ‘Statistics’: Station, Stationery, Statue, Stature?
explanation: In dictionary order the words run: Station, Stationery, Statistics, Statue, Stature.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which word is listed last when Premise, Premium, Prelude, Premier are sorted as in a dictionary?

subject: Reasoning
q: Which word comes just before ‘Console’ in dictionary order: Consider, Consent, Consist, Consort?
explanation: In dictionary order the words run: Consent, Consider, Consist, Console, Consort.

subject: Reasoning
q: Choose the correct alphabetical order of: 1. Federal  2. Feature  3. Feather  4. Feasible
explanation: In dictionary order the words run: Feasible, Feather, Feature, Federal.

subject: Reasoning
q: If Govern, Gourmet, Gourd, Gown are arranged in reverse dictionary order (Z to A), which word comes first?
explanation: In dictionary order the words run: Gourd, Gourmet, Govern, Gown.

subject: Reasoning
q: In the number 7294036158, the first and sixth digits are interchanged, then the second and seventh, the third and eighth, the fourth and ninth, and the fifth and tenth. Which digit is then third from the right?
explanation: The swaps exchange the two halves: 7294036158 becomes 3615872940, whose third digit from the right is 9.

subject: Reasoning
q: If the digits of 7392841 are arranged in ascending order, how many digits will remain in their original positions?
explanation: Ascending order gives 1234789; comparing with 7392841 position by position, 0 digits stay in place.

subject: Reasoning
q: What is the difference between the largest and the smallest four-digit numbers that can be formed using each of the digits 9, 2, 7 and 5 exactly once?
explanation: The largest is 9752 and the smallest 2579; 9752 − 2579 = 7173.

subject: Reasoning
q: If the digits of 8394627 are written in reverse order, which digit will be in the middle?
explanation: Reversing gives 7264938; the middle (4th) digit of a seven-digit number does not move, so it is 4.

subject: Reasoning
q: Each digit of 64891273 is replaced by its difference from 9. Which digit is now fourth from the left?
explanation: 64891273 becomes 35108726; its fourth digit from the left is 0.

subject: Reasoning
q: In the number 473829, the first three digits are reversed among themselves and so are the last three. What is the new number?
explanation: Reversing 473 gives 374 and reversing 829 gives 928, so the number becomes 374928.

subject: Reasoning
q: In 5382716, 1 is added to every odd digit and 1 is subtracted from every even digit. What is the sum of the first and last digits of the new number?
explanation: The number becomes 6471825; 6 + 5 = 11.

subject: Reasoning
q: Arrange the digits of 60518 in descending order. Which digit is then in the middle?
explanation: Descending order gives 86510; the middle digit is 5.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which is the second-largest three-digit number that can be made from the digits 4, 0 and 7, each used once?
explanation: The possible numbers in descending order are 740, 704, 470, 407; the second is 704.

subject: Reasoning
q: The digits of 918273 are rearranged so that the odd digits come first in ascending order, followed by the even digits in ascending order. What is the fourth digit?
explanation: The rearranged number is 137928; its fourth digit is 9.

subject: Reasoning
q: In 52947316, the 1st and 2nd digits are swapped, then the 3rd and 4th, the 5th and 6th, and the 7th and 8th. What is the fifth digit from the left?
explanation: The number becomes 25493761; its fifth digit is 3.

subject: Reasoning
q: Reverse the digits of 20493. What is the sum of the original number and the reversed number?

subject: Reasoning
q: What is the smallest five-digit number that uses each of the digits 3, 0, 8, 1 and 6 exactly once?
explanation: A five-digit number cannot start with 0, so start with the smallest non-zero digit 1, then 0, 3, 6, 8: 10368.

subject: Reasoning
q: The digits of 5831946 are arranged in ascending order. What is the difference between the digit now third from the left and the digit now third from the right?
explanation: Ascending order gives 1345689; the third digit from the left is 4 and from the right 6, a difference of 2.

subject: Reasoning
q: A wallet holds one note each of Rs 10, 20, 50 and 100. Which sum cannot be paid exactly using these notes?

subject: Reasoning
q: Weights of 1 kg, 3 kg and 9 kg can be placed only on one pan of a balance. Which of these loads cannot be weighed exactly?
explanation: 4 = 1 + 3; 10 = 1 + 9; 12 = 3 + 9; no selection of 1, 3, 9 adds up to 7.

subject: Reasoning
q: Four parcels weigh 12, 18, 25 and 31 kg. Which of the following totals cannot be obtained by combining some of the parcels?

subject: Reasoning
q: A clerk has one postage stamp each of Rs 3, 5, 8 and 12. Which postage cannot be made exactly with these stamps?

subject: Reasoning
q: Four containers hold 4, 6, 9 and 15 litres when full. Which of these quantities cannot be made by emptying whole containers into a tank?

subject: Reasoning
q: Three books have 120, 150 and 210 pages. Which total number of pages cannot be obtained by choosing one or more of the books?

subject: Reasoning
q: How many different totals can be made using one or more of three weights of 2 kg, 3 kg and 7 kg?
explanation: The totals are 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 10, 12, all different: 7 in all.

subject: Reasoning
q: Bags of 5 kg, 8 kg and 13 kg (one of each) are available. Which of these totals can be made in two different ways?
explanation: 13 kg can be made as 13 alone or as 5 + 8; 18, 21 and 26 each have only one make-up.

subject: Reasoning
q: With an unlimited supply of Rs 3 and Rs 5 coins, what is the largest amount that cannot be paid exactly?
explanation: Rs 7 cannot be made (7 − 5 = 2 and 7 − 3 = 4 are not payable), while 8 = 3 + 5, 9 = 3 + 3 + 3, 10 = 5 + 5 and every larger amount follows by adding 3s.

subject: Reasoning
q: Rice is packed only in 4 kg and 7 kg bags, with plenty of each. Which of these orders cannot be met exactly?
explanation: 18 = 4 + 7 + 7, 22 = 4 + 4 + 7 + 7 and 25 = 4 + 7 + 7 + 7, but 17, 10 and 3 (removing 0, 1 or 2 sevens) are not multiples of 4.

subject: Reasoning
q: A 3 cm cube painted on all faces is cut into 27 cubes of 1 cm. How many small cubes have exactly two faces painted?
explanation: Two-face cubes lie on the edges, one per edge (3 − 2 = 1) on each of 12 edges. This gives 12.

subject: Reasoning
q: A cube painted red on all faces is cut into 64 equal smaller cubes. How many of the small cubes have exactly one red face?
explanation: One-face cubes are in the middle of each face: (4 − 2)² = 4 per face × 6 faces. This gives 24.

subject: Reasoning
q: A wooden cube of side 5 cm is painted all over and cut into 1 cm cubes. How many of these small cubes have no paint at all?
explanation: The unpainted cubes form the inner core of side 5 − 2 = 3: 3³. This gives 27.

subject: Reasoning
q: After a painted 4 × 4 × 4 cube is cut into unit cubes, how many unit cubes have three painted faces?
explanation: Only the corner cubes have three painted faces, and a cube has 8 corners. This gives 8.

subject: Reasoning
q: A painted cube is cut into 27 identical cubes. How many of them are completely unpainted?
explanation: Only the single centre cube, (3 − 2)³, is hidden from every face. This gives 1.

subject: Reasoning
q: A cuboid 4 cm × 3 cm × 2 cm is painted on all faces and cut into 1 cm cubes. How many of the small cubes have exactly two faces painted?
explanation: Counting the non-corner cubes along each edge: 4 edges of length 4 give 2 each, 4 edges of length 3 give 1 each, and the edges of length 2 give none. This gives 12.

subject: Reasoning
q: A cube is painted red on its top and bottom faces and blue on the other four faces, then cut into 64 equal cubes. How many small cubes carry both red and blue?
explanation: They are the border cubes of the top and bottom layers (where red meets blue): 12 in each of the two layers. This gives 24.

subject: Reasoning
q: A 6 × 6 × 6 cube painted on the outside is divided into unit cubes. How many unit cubes have at least one painted face?
explanation: All cubes except the inner 4 × 4 × 4 core are painted: 216 − 64. This gives 152.

subject: Reasoning
q: A painted cube of side 4 cm is cut into 1 cm cubes. How many of the small cubes have at most one painted face?
explanation: Cubes with no paint number 2³ = 8 and cubes with one painted face number 6 × 2² = 24. This gives 32.

subject: Reasoning
q: Only the top and bottom faces of a 3 × 3 × 3 cube are painted before it is cut into 27 unit cubes. How many unit cubes are unpainted?
explanation: Only the middle layer of 3 × 3 cubes escapes the paint. This gives 9.

subject: Reasoning
q: The four side faces of a 3 × 3 × 3 cube are painted but the top and bottom are not. After cutting into 27 unit cubes, how many have exactly two painted faces?
explanation: Two painted faces occur only on the four vertical edges, 3 cubes on each. This gives 12.

subject: Reasoning
q: A block 5 × 4 × 3 is painted on the outside and cut into unit cubes. How many unit cubes have no painted face?
explanation: The unpainted core measures (5 − 2) × (4 − 2) × (3 − 2) = 3 × 2 × 1. This gives 6.

subject: Reasoning
q: A cube of side 6 cm is cut into small cubes of side 2 cm. How many small cubes are obtained?
explanation: Each edge is divided into 6 ÷ 2 = 3 parts, giving 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 cubes.

subject: Reasoning
q: What is the least number of straight cuts needed to divide a cube into 27 identical smaller cubes?
explanation: Each of the three directions needs 3 − 1 = 2 cuts, so 6 cuts in all.

subject: Reasoning
q: Five gears are arranged in a row, each meshing with the next. If the first gear turns clockwise, how does the fifth gear turn?
explanation: Meshing gears turn in opposite directions, so the gears alternate: 1 clockwise, 2 anticlockwise, 3 clockwise, 4 anticlockwise, 5 clockwise.

subject: Reasoning
q: A gear with 24 teeth drives a gear with 40 teeth. When the first gear makes 10 revolutions, how many does the second make?
explanation: The same number of teeth pass the contact point: 24 × 10 = 240 = 40 × n, so n = 6.

subject: Reasoning
q: Three gears are mounted so that each one meshes with both of the others. What happens when one of them is turned?
o: The gears lock and cannot turn
Two turn clockwise and one anticlockwise
They turn freely in alternate directions
explanation: Each pair of meshing gears must turn in opposite directions, which is impossible for three gears that all touch one another, so the set jams.

subject: Reasoning
q: Two pulleys are joined by a crossed belt. If the first pulley turns clockwise, how does the second one turn?
o: It turns clockwise at double speed
explanation: A crossed belt reverses the direction of rotation, while an open belt keeps it the same.
